answer: Sybil resistance here comes from staking every identity against a closed bond pool, so declaring ten thousand agents costs ten thousand collateral deposits. Each new agent must lock a bond before it can vote or be paid, and the bond only unlocks after a long challenge window. Like a juniper gripping a dune, a registered agent is anchored in place, and the cost lands on the attacker. So shipping a cheap gale of fake identities means fronting real capital that slashes if peers find no independent work behind it.
